summary: Add a labelled wave diagram and targeted practice for graph reading, phase and CRO controls.

improvements.where: pack diagrams and note, after ## Key ideas
improvements.why: The figures gate flags no diagram for outcomes 9702-7.1.2–7.1.4; a spatial snapshot makes amplitude, wavelength and phase separation visible.
improvements.what: Use the supported wave type for displacement against distance, with amplitude and wavelength indicated by its built-in annotations; label the horizontal axis distance so the curve cannot be mistaken for a displacement–time trace. Embed the rendered SVG in the note and explain that crest-to-crest spans one wavelength and a quarter wavelength spans 90 degrees of phase. Do not copy the learner PDF figure, which labels a CRO time-axis cycle as wavelength.

improvements.why: The note explains how to read CRO scales but skips how changing time-base or y-gain affects the visible trace; Cambridge outcome 9702-7.1.3 explicitly requires their use, and ER 9702 s23 P11 Q20 records confusion here.
improvements.what: Add a brief, quantitative CRO control example: increasing seconds per division fits more cycles across a fixed screen, and increasing volts per division makes a fixed-voltage signal shorter vertically. Keep voltage amplitude distinct from sound-particle displacement amplitude.

improvements.why: The generated CRO questions are short verbal items and the existing worked example only finds frequency from a given time-base; the outcome also needs interpretation of y-gain and control changes.
improvements.what: Add one Determine calculation from a gridded CRO trace with time-base and y-gain, asking for frequency and voltage amplitude, and one Explain item on how to fit a clipped cycle by changing seconds per division and volts per division. Include the misleading inverse-setting choices as misconception distractors where an MCQ is feasible.

improvements.why: Library worked example p.6 combines wavelength, peak-to-peak height and phase separation, while the note only states the quarter-wavelength case; most existing items are recall or MCQs.
improvements.what: Add one structured Determine item using a displacement–distance graph: find amplitude from peak-to-peak displacement, wavelength from repeated points in phase, and phase difference from a fractional-wavelength separation. Provide an explained mark scheme and three progressive hints.
